The NYT reports that powerful synthetic drugs produced in small labs are becoming a major force in today's illegal drug market. The lesson is simple: prohibition doesn’t stop drugs—it makes them stronger, riskier, and more deadly, says Cato’s @dr4liberty. 
ow.ly/b2B450YHapT

The new Section 122 tariffs are just as illegal as the previous ones, and for many of the same reasons, explains Cato’s @Thomas_A_Berry.
cato.org/blog/new-tariffs-ar…

We’ve warned since 1991 that there’s a disconnect between what students learn in school and what skills they’ll need to thrive as citizens and workers. Those warnings have resulted in buzzwords and reports but little substantive reform. 

The AI economic transition already underway demands a broader and sustained response per Cato’s @KevinTFrazier.
cato.org/commentary/weve-bee…

Autism diagnoses are rising—but much of it may be overdiagnosis. A broken Medicaid system rewards more labels and more therapy, driving billions in waste, fraud, and care that doesn’t always help the kids who need it most, report Cato’s @AdamOmaryPhD and @dr4liberty.
ow.ly/oFbY50YEvGn

Ludwig von Mises, one of the 20th century’s foremost champions of free markets, saw clearly that socialism isn’t merely inefficient—it’s inherently destructive. Decades of failed central planning have made his case undeniable.

The federal government confiscated $5.23 trillion of Americans’ money in fiscal year 2025 – but it’s not enough to cover the $7 trillion Congress spent, Cato’s @adamnmichel and @SantiagoForster report. 
  
Here are five charts that break down who pays and how much, and why today's spending puts future taxes at risk:  
ow.ly/feZ450YHibF

Arizona’s HB 2415 would effectively ban 7‑OH products based on rare overdose reports—often involving multiple substances. That could push chronic pain patients to black markets or fentanyl-laced opioids. Regulate potency & labeling, don’t prohibit painkillers, says @dr4liberty. 
ow.ly/gvhb50YH9hX

Virginia's hemp crackdown won't make consumers safer. It'll just make their choices more dangerous. That's not public safety — it's prohibition with a new name, explains Cato’s @dr4liberty. 
  
ow.ly/Pkta50YHhMS

An Arizona mom grew a 7-student pandemic microschool into 8 K–8 sites, plus virtual and high school programs—about 10 students each. 

The model is expanding access and creating jobs but also drawing legal pushback from local public schools. Learn more from @ColleenHroncich.
ow.ly/uQP050YEAqn

The Cato Institute and Professor Ilya Somin have filed an amicus brief in the US Court of International Trade arguing that Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 cannot lawfully be used to impose tariffs under current circumstances. 
 
 “The president’s interpretation of this law is a sweeping power grab that would enable him to impose massive tariffs up to 15%, almost anytime he wants,” says @IlyaSomin.
 
ow.ly/wqwG50YHf3c

The FBI is reportedly labeling frequent FOIA requesters as “vexsome,” creating a de facto blacklist. That’s a clear violation of the letter and spirit of the FOIA statute that federal courts and Congress should punish, says Cato’s @PGEddington.
ow.ly/qVZ750YGJ4e

Senator Warren is targeting MrBeast over his new finance app, but this isn’t about protecting kids—it’s about policing innovation. Jimmy Donaldson built his brand on helping people, and youth banking tools already exist. Washington shouldn’t scare off new competition.

ow.ly/C81M50YGGv1

Section 122 is inapplicable and inappropriate for the types of tariffs the administration is imposing, says @RepJimmyPanetta at a Cato Institute event.  
    
Watch the full event here: ow.ly/zWJw50YG047

Video

Senator Warren's childcare bill doesn't make care cheaper—it makes taxpayers cover yet higher costs. Deregulation, not subsidies, would expand supply and bring prices down, explain Cato’s @MrRBourne and Nathan Miller.

ow.ly/x7Ep50YFOui

The DOJ declared the Presidential Records Act unconstitutional, meaning a president can treat official records as personal property and destroy them. This amounts to a radical reduction in legal accountability, argues Cato’s Patrick G. Eddington.

ow.ly/JFmH50YFPWP

With South Carolina’s Education Scholarship Trust Fund, parents can customize their kids’ education. There are similar programs in 16 other states. This isn’t a loophole—it’s the program working as designed, says Cato’s @ColleenHroncich. 
ow.ly/ZeoO50YEA63

Trump’s Maritime Action Plan aims to revive US shipbuilding with subsidies and mandates. But US-built ships cost about 5x global prices, and shipyards face labor and supply chain shortages exacerbated by US immigration restrictions and tariffs. 

Protectionism won’t make them competitive—or fix naval shipbuilding, says Cato’s @cpgrabow. 
ow.ly/eYoM50YEzIh

The answer to Washington’s affordability crisis isn’t more government intervention—it's less. The better path is sound money and more economic freedom to supply everything from housing and childcare to energy and food.

Video

Hungary has been a “laboratory” for illiberal nationalism under Viktor Orbán, Cato’s @johanknorberg explains. After 16 years: weaker checks and balances, a steep press-freedom slide, and a poorer, less free country—hardly the promised model. 

Learn more: 
ow.ly/jen750YGGFg

FCC Chairman Carr's pressure on CNN—whatever you think of their war reporting—is the latest alarming example of government officials trying to shape news coverage, says Cato’s @bskorup. The real fix: strip the FCC of the vague authority that makes these threats possible. 

ow.ly/Qfa550YGKUT
